# situation: on pull_request, a job runs make on a runner labelled
#   self-hosted and linux, in a private or internal repository that lets
#   those who may read it fork it and runs the workflows of pull requests
#   from its forks (repo.public false, repo.allow-forking true,
#   repo.fork-pr-run-workflows true).
# reason: on pull_request, GitHub runs the workflow file as the pull request
#   has it, so one who may read the repository and fork it (every member of
#   the enterprise reads an internal one) can rewrite the steps, and
#   runs-on: [self-hosted, linux] sends them to the repository's own runner.
# attack: one who may read the repository forks it and opens a pull request
#   whose copy of this workflow runs a step of their own in place of make.
# attack-run-behavior: the setting Run workflows from fork pull requests is
#   on, so the pull request's run starts; the job a runs the attacker's step
#   on a runner of the repository with both labels, where what it leaves
#   stays for the jobs that run there after it, with their secrets and
#   tokens.
on: workflow_call
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]
    steps:
      - run: make
